memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Joshua saved them from the Israelites, and they did not kill them. That day he made the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the assembly, to provide for the needs of the altar of the Lord at the place the Lord would choose. And that is what they are to this day. — Josh 9:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with mercy. "Joshua saved them from the Israelites, and they did not kill them." The Gibeonites, who deserved nothing and had earned only distrust through their deceit, are spared and given a lasting place among God's people. And that place, though humble, was one of remarkable privilege: they would "provide for the needs of the altar of the Lord." The very centre of Israel's worship became the focus of their service.

Think of the grace in this. These outsiders, these deceivers, these Canaanites under God's judgment, end up serving at the altar of the Lord. What began in fear and deception ends in a permanent place near the worship of the true God. The phrase "to this day" tells us this was no temporary arrangement; the Gibeonites became a lasting part of the community, bound to the service of God's house.

This is one of those quiet moments in the Old Testament where the wideness of God's mercy shines through. Alongside Rahab the Canaanite, the Gibeonites are outsiders drawn into the life of God's people. God's grace was never meant to stay locked within one nation; from the beginning it reached out to gather in the unlikely and the undeserving.

This points forward to the gospel, in which people from every nation are brought near through Christ. We who were once "far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ" (Eph 2:13). Like the Gibeonites, we came as outsiders with nothing to offer but our need. And in mercy, God has not only spared us but given us a place in His house, near His altar, to serve Him forever. That is the astonishing reach of His grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the mercy shown to the Gibeonites deepen your wonder at God's grace to outsiders?
2. How does it move you that you, once "far away," have been brought near through Christ?
3. Are you serving God with gratitude for the place He has given you in His house?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the wideness of Your mercy that reaches even outsiders like me. I was far away, but through Christ You have brought me near and given me a place to serve You. Amen.
